titulo: Study Guide 1 — Reading a story, past simple and plurals

bloques.titulo: What you will learn this week

bloques.html:
• Read a short story and answer questions about what happened (literal) and why it happened (inferential).
  • Put the events of a story in order (sequence).
  • Describe a character with a trait word (brave, kind, shy, grateful...).
  • Use the past simple correctly: regular verbs (-ed) and irregular verbs (went, saw, took...).
  • Form plurals, including the tricky ones (children, leaves, mice).
  • Listen to a story read aloud and answer questions; tell your own story with a beginning, a middle and an end.

Reading a story

A story has characters (who), a setting (where and when) and a plot (what happens). The plot usually has a beginning (we meet the characters), a middle (a problem appears) and an end (the problem is solved).

There are two kinds of questions:

Kind of question How to answer it Example
Literal ("right there") Find the words in the text. Where did Tomás go? → "to the lake"
Inferential ("think and search") Use clues from the text + what you know. The answer is not written, but the text proves it. Why did his face turn red? → He was embarrassed, because he had said fishing was boring.

Character traits are words that describe how a person is, not how they look: brave, honest, patient, stubborn, generous, curious, grateful, selfish, shy, cheerful. To find a trait, look at what the character does and says.

Grammar box — Past simple

Regular verbs add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, want → wanted. - Ends in e: add only -d: live → lived, dance → danced. - Consonant + y: change y to -ied: carry → carried, study → studied. - Short verb, one vowel + one consonant: double the consonant: stop → stopped, plan → planned.

Irregular verbs change completely. Learn these 20:

go → went see → saw take → took eat → ate run → ran
come → came give → gave make → made find → found lose → lost
buy → bought think → thought fall → fell write → wrote have → had
say → said tell → told get → got know → knew begin → began

Negative and questions use did + base verb: She didn't go. Did you see it? (never "didn't went").

Plurals

  • Most nouns: +s → dogs, mittens.
  • Ends in -s, -x, -ch, -sh: +es → boxes, buses, watches, wishes.
  • Consonant + y → -ies: baby → babies, story → stories (but day → days).
  • -f / -fe → -ves: leaf → leaves, knife → knives, wolf → wolves.
  • Irregular: child → children, mouse → mice, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people, man → men, woman → women, sheep → sheep, fish → fish.

Vocabulary of the week

Word Meaning Word Meaning
mitten a glove with one space for the thumb and one for all the other fingers scarf a long piece of cloth you wear around your neck
knit to make clothes by joining wool with two long needles crunch the noise snow or dry leaves make when you step on them
dare (someone) to challenge someone to do something risky or silly bare not covered; a bare hand has no glove
concentrate to put all your attention on one thing snowbank a pile of snow pushed to the side of a road or path
scan to look quickly but carefully over an area to find something whole complete, with nothing missing or broken
grateful feeling thankful embarrassed feeling shy or uncomfortable because of something you did
trout a fish that lives in rivers and lakes rod a long thin stick used for fishing
grab to take something quickly with your hand slide to move smoothly over a surface
suddenly quickly and without warning at last finally, after waiting a long time
stubborn not willing to change your mind patient able to wait calmly without getting angry

Read this short story and look at how each question is answered.

The Bike Lesson

Camila was eight when her father took the training wheels off her bike. "You're ready," he said. Camila was not sure. She pushed the pedals, wobbled, and fell on the grass. She got up and tried again. She fell again. Her knee hurt and her eyes filled with tears, but she did not say a word. She climbed back on. On the fifth try, the bike went straight for ten meters before she fell. On the sixth try, it didn't fall at all. Her father ran behind her, shouting and laughing. That night Camila put a bandage on her knee and smiled at it in the mirror.

Example 1 (literal). How old was Camila? → Find it in the text: "Camila was eight". Answer: eight.

Example 2 (sequence). What happened right after she fell the first time? → Look at the order of sentences: "She got up and tried again." Answer: she tried again.

Example 3 (character trait). Which word describes Camila: lazy, stubborn or shy? → She fell many times but "climbed back on" and "did not say a word". She refuses to give up. Answer: stubborn (in a good way: determined).

Example 4 (inferential). Why did Camila smile at the bandage? → The text does not say. Clues: the bandage came from falling, and falling was part of learning. She is proud of what she achieved. Answer: because the bandage reminded her she had learned to ride; she was proud.

Example 5 (past simple). Yesterday I (go) to the park and (play) football. → go is irregular → went; play is regular → played.

Example 6 (negative). She didn't (see) the dog. → After didn't use the base form: see (not "saw").

Example 7 (plural). one wolf → two → ends in -f → wolves.

Read the story and answer questions 1 to 6.

The Red Kite

Every Sunday, Diego and his grandmother walked to the hill behind their house in Puerto Varas to fly a kite. Diego's kite was red with a long yellow tail. One windy Sunday in October, the string broke. The kite rose higher and higher and disappeared behind the trees.

Diego sat down on the grass and did not speak. His grandmother sat beside him. "Kites are made to fly," she said. "That one just flew a little farther than usual."

They walked home in silence. On Monday, Diego came home from school and found a box on his bed. Inside was a new kite, blue this time, and a note: "This one has a stronger string. Sunday?"

Diego ran to the kitchen and hugged his grandmother so hard that she dropped a spoon.
Where did Diego and his grandmother fly the kite?
What color was the first kite?
What happened on the windy Sunday in October?
Number these events in order (1-4): Diego finds a box on his bed. The string breaks. Diego hugs his grandmother. Diego sits on the grass without speaking.
Which word best describes the grandmother: strict, generous or careless? Explain with one detail from the text.
Why did Diego hug his grandmother so hard? (This is an inference: the text does not say it directly.)
Grammar.
Write the past simple: a) walk → b) stop → c) carry → d) live →
Write the past simple: a) go → b) eat → c) buy → d) fall → e) write →
Complete: Last winter we (make) a snowman and my brother (lose) his hat in the snow.
Correct the mistake: I didn't went to school yesterday.
Write the plural: a) box → b) story → c) leaf → d) child → e) tooth →
Which is correct? a) three mouses / three mice b) two foots / two feet c) many persons / many people
Writing.
Write 4 sentences about something you did last weekend. Use at least four past simple verbs. Start with "Last weekend..." and finish with how you felt.
Listening and speaking practice (ask an adult).
Ask an adult to read you any short story aloud twice. After listening, tell them: who the characters were, where it happened, and the beginning, middle and end in order.
Tell a two-minute story about a time you lost something. Use First..., Then..., Finally... and say how you felt at the end.
1. On the hill behind their house in Puerto Varas.
1. Red (with a yellow tail).
1. The string broke and the kite flew away behind the trees.
1. Generous: she bought him a new kite (also kind/understanding: "Kites are made to fly").
1. Because he was grateful and happy: she had understood how sad he was and bought him a new kite with a stronger string.
1. a) walked b) stopped c) carried d) lived.
1. a) went b) ate c) bought d) fell e) wrote.
1. made · lost.
1. I didn't go to school yesterday.
1. a) boxes b) stories c) leaves d) children e) teeth.
1. a) three mice b) two feet c) many people.
1. Check: four sentences, verbs in the past (walked, went, played, saw...), a feeling at the end (I was happy / tired / proud).
Items 14 and 15: check with the adult. Did you say who, where, and the three parts in order?
